solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Still recalling cream lace bra cups

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters picked out are read backwards
the bra cups, or holds, a run of letters spread across these three words

explanation.surface: Lingerie shopping: a cream lace bra whose cups bring something to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' takes MLACEB from cream lace bra, and 'recalling' turns it round. 'Still' looks like an adverb but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To becalm a ship is to leave it motionless for want of wind, so the verb means to make quiet or motionless.

clue.text: Strongly advise other doctors compromising vote

indicators.note: the vote mark sits inside, compromising the jumbled word
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Different physicians are accused of tampering with a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctors' looks like a noun but is the verb tamper with, turning OTHER into EHORT; 'compromising' puts X inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to exhort is to urge earnestly, to press someone to act.

clue.text: Article about one way and another to serve up stimulant

indicators.note: the article goes around the rest

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means read upwards, so these pieces run backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a lane is a narrow road, a way
RD, the abbreviation for road, is another way

explanation.surface: Instructions for presenting a pick-me-up, using an item and some routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to serve up' only turns the three pieces for one, way and another; 'another' way is the road abbreviation. The article then wraps round the reversed run.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrenalin is the hormone that excites the body, a natural stimulant.

clue.text: In revolution, honour cold royal in a snide manner

indicators.note: turning around means the award letters are read backwards

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
kingly means regal, royal

explanation.surface: During an uprising, a chilly monarch is decorated amid sneering.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour awarded by the monarch; 'In revolution' turns only its abbreviation, not the cold or royal pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mockingly means with derision, in a sneering, scornful way.

clue.text: Made out only to settle again

parts.note: to make out writing is to read it
just means merely, only

explanation.surface: Someone made a cheque out solely in order to settle a bill a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to readjust is to adjust or set right once more.

clue.text: Gain new skills on public transport

parts.note: re means on, regarding
a train is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Someone learns a fresh trade while commuting by rail.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrain is to undergo training again, learning different work skills.

clue.text: When guards save borders

indicators.note: the word for when surrounds the word for save

parts.note: as means when, while
but means except, save

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper defends while making a save near the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' is the preposition meaning except, BUT, not a goalkeeper's stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to abut is to adjoin, to lie next to along a boundary.

clue.text: Country where first of two vessels is docked

indicators.note: the first vessel has its tail cut off, as a dog's tail is docked

parts.note: a jar is a container
a pan is a cooking vessel

explanation.surface: A port where the leading one of a pair of ships has come in to berth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' says which vessel 'is docked': JAR loses its last letter. 'docked' suggests ships but means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is an island country of East Asia.

clue.text: Female wearing outfit is pressed in

indicators.note: the team word goes around the female, like clothing

parts.note: a squad is a team or outfit
she is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman in a smart costume is being ironed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outfit' looks like clothing but is a group of people, SQUAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Squashed means crushed or flattened, pressed in.

clue.text: Quicker way to get Brie, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a quicker route than the usual one
the word brief with its last letter lopped off becomes Brie, so it is an example of a word cut short

explanation.surface: Advice on the fastest way to obtain some soft French cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: Brie is the soft French cheese, but here it is just the word brief with its end cut off, a short cut of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a short cut is a route that saves time compared with the normal way.

clue.text: Remove power from group of countries, with publicity

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, a body of member countries
a plug is a piece of promotion for a product

explanation.surface: A bloc of nations cuts off a country's electricity while drawing press attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To unplug a device is to disconnect it from its electricity supply.

clue.text: Britain's ancient symbol associated with island nation

parts.note: B is a standard abbreviation for Britain or British
a rune is a letter of the old Germanic alphabet

explanation.surface: A historic British emblem is linked with some island country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'island nation' tempts as one definition, but Brunei is a state on Borneo; 'island' gives I and 'nation' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunei is an independent sultanate in South-East Asia, a sovereign country.

clue.text: Boy is getting into craft that is lighter

indicators.note: the pair of pieces goes inside the word for craft

parts.note: art means skill or craft
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A lad joins in some handiwork, which makes him feel less burdened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' reads as a comparative of light (less heavy) but is someone who lights things, deliberately.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsonist sets fires deliberately, a criminal fire-starter, cryptically one who lights.

clue.text: Bladed implement decapitating swine

indicators.note: cutting off the head removes the first letter

parts.note: a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A tool with a blade is used to behead a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bladed implement' suggests an axe, but rowers' oars have blades too.
explanation.definitionFit: An oar is a pole with a flat blade, used to row a boat.

clue.text: Fruit bats so near gerbil

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Flying mammals and a small rodent nest close together among the berries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the animals but is the anagram signal on SO NEAR GERBIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Loganberries are a hybrid soft fruit, a cross between raspberry and blackberry.

clue.text: No longer thoughtful, dear?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: A partner asks whether their beloved has stopped being considerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dear' reads as an endearment but means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dear in the sense of high-priced, costly.

clue.text: Kingdom's fruitarians peeled bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters are mixed up
the outer letters are stripped off like skin

explanation.surface: A realm whose fruit-only eaters have skinned some bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' strips F and S off fruitarians; 'bananas' shuffles RUITARIAN. Ruritania is the imaginary kingdom of Anthony Hope's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the fictional central European kingdom of The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Supporters of sportsperson, Europeans backing runner

indicators.note: the word for Europeans comes behind the runner

parts.note: a ski is a runner, like that of a sledge
Poles are people from Poland

explanation.surface: Fans of an athlete include continental visitors who bet on a racer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete but is the long blade a sledge or skier slides on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ski poles are the sticks a skier leans on, so they literally hold up a sportsperson.

clue.text: Thin bird, one barely in the water

parts.note: skinny means very thin
the dipper is a small bird of fast streams

explanation.surface: A slender wading bird stands almost naked in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' means only just, but here it is bare, naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who swims naked; 'barely' is a pun on bare, without clothes.

clue.text: Assume upset will provide positive sign

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upwards, reversed

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on, assume them

explanation.surface: Taking it that someone is upset will produce an encouraging sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod of the head signals agreement, an affirmative gesture.

clue.text: Stop dinosaur's admission

definitions.meaning: a dinosaur, an out-of-date person, would confess to being old hat, out of fashion

explanation.walkthrough: A 'dinosaur' is someone old-fashioned; read as I'M PASSÉ the answer is their confession.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock where progress halts, a standstill.

clue.text: Engineering on grey hydraulic structure

indicators.note: engineering means contriving, so the letters are re-arranged

explanation.surface: A grey concrete structure built to control water.
explanation.walkthrough: A groyne is a low wall built out from a beach to stop sand drifting.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a sea-defence barrier built into the water to check erosion.

clue.text: Puts one's foot down when finding drug and drink

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
to sup is to sip or drink

explanation.surface: Someone takes a firm stand on discovering narcotics and alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts one's foot down' sounds like being firm, but it is pressing the accelerator.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to put your foot down in a car is to accelerate, to go faster.

clue.text: Continually holding line to get fish

indicators.note: the word for always contains the line letter

parts.note: ever means always, continually

explanation.surface: An angler keeps a line in the water constantly to catch something.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a fish.

clue.text: Resentment between partners causes alarm

indicators.note: the anger word sits between the two bridge letters

parts.note: in bridge, South and North are partners, S and N
ire means anger, resentment

explanation.surface: Bitterness within a couple is causing anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partners' suggests a couple; it is the bridge partners North and South, S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a loud warning device, an alarm.

clue.text: Official shop's back yard

indicators.note: back means the phrase for shop is read backwards

parts.note: to shop someone is to rat on them, inform on them to the police

explanation.surface: An officer is found in the yard behind a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shop' is the British slang verb for informing on someone, RAT ON; 'back' turns it into NOTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a public official who certifies documents and witnesses signatures.

clue.text: Chef has duck, food rich in protein

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the figure 0, so O
liver is offal, high in protein

explanation.surface: A cook prepares a duck dish with a protein-rich accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' suggests a duck dish; it is a zero score, O. Jamie Oliver is a well-known British TV chef.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamie Oliver is a famous British celebrity cook, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Possessing passion, cuts back collection of plants

definitions.note: plural answer: each spinney is a small wood, so plants collected; the clue treats several of them loosely

indicators.note: the whole assembly is read backwards
the word for cuts holds the word for passion inside it

parts.note: snips are small cuts
a yen is a strong longing

explanation.surface: A gardener, gripped by enthusiasm, prunes the shrubbery hard.
explanation.walkthrough: SNIPS holding YEN gives SYENNIPS, which 'back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinney is a small copse of trees and undergrowth, a grouping of growing things.

clue.text: Sergeant at sea is cut off

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A naval sergeant is isolated far from shore.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to alienate them, to sever them from family or friends.

clue.text: Overjoyed when told leader's dismissed

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for told is removed

parts.note: to relate a story is to tell it

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled on hearing that the boss has been fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: elated means jubilant, in high spirits.
